content.text: Hi Quinn, you are correct. I have no excuse but would draw your attention to the PR where we did some discussion about this and outlined our reasoning.
If you’d like to come to the call this Thursday at 10am ET we’d love to hear your use case.
Thanks for the comment.  I’ll add that meeting to my schedule and try to attend.  I did read the PR before and while personally, I’m a little concerned about how
can seem to represent different things based on what your
ing to, for this issue, I’m more concerned that for the binary resource
in the GET request, which I don’t see how that’s part of the discussion for in  that previous PR.
Ohhhhh, sorry I must have missed that. Okay I see what you are saying, I’ll have a look.

The LDP specification indicates that any subject should allowed as statements in any LDP Resource (LDPR).  This functionality isn't consistent between containers (which seem to work) and binary resources (which don't).  In particular, binary resources seem to transfer all statements from a metadata record into the subject of the resource itself.
This example applies the same metadata, that includes a label for an subject term, to both a container and a binary resource:

version=6.3.0-SNAPSHOT
     docker image pull fcrepo/fcrepo:$version
     docker image list fcrepo/fcrepo:$version
     echo -e "\n\n"

     docker run --rm --name=fcrepo --publish 8666:8080 fcrepo/fcrepo:latest 2>fcrepo.err >fcrepo.log &
     sleep 5

     info_fedora='http://localhost:8666/fcrepo/rest'
     ttl='
         @prefix ldp:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#> .
         @prefix schema: <http://schema.org/> .
         @prefix wiki: <http://en.wikipedia.org/> .
         <>  schema:name "Ashley";
             schema:about wiki:Cat;
              .

         wiki:Cat schema:name "Cat".
         ';

     ashley='
          \    /\
           )  ( `)
          (  /  )
           \(__)|
     ';
     curl -XPUT -u fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -H'Content-type:text/turtle' --data-binary "@-" $info_fedora/ashley <<< "$ttl"
     curl -XPUT -u fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -H'Content-type:text/x-ascii-art' --data-binary "@-" $info_fedora/ashley.art <<< "$ashley"
     curl -XPUT -u fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -H'Content-type:text/turtle' --data-binary "@-" $info_fedora/ashley.art/fcr:metadata <<< "$ttl"

     echo -e "\n========= LDP ========\n"
     for i in ashley.art ashley.art/fcr:metadata ashley; do
         echo "========== $i =========="
         curl -u fedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin -H'PREFER:return=representation; omit="http://fedora.info/definitions/fcrepo#ServerManaged"' $info_fedora/$i
         echo -e "========== $i ==========\n"

     done
     echo -e "\n========= OCFL ========\n"
     echo "========== ashley.art~fcr-desc.nt =========="
     docker exec fcrepo cat fcrepo-home/data/ocfl-root/889/c1a/e3f/889c1ae3f46c7952fd40cd139ee5a6225654f659913aba5d2de2533c1841d3fa/v2/content/ashley.art~fcr-desc.nt
     echo -e "========== ashley.art~fcr-desc.nt ==========\n"

     docker stop fcrepo > /dev/null

Hi Quinn, you are correct. I have no excuse but would draw your attention to the PR where we did some discussion about this and outlined our reasoning. https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/pull/1988

If you’d like to come to the call this Thursday at 10am ET we’d love to hear your use case. https://wiki.lyrasis.org/display/FF/2022-10-27+-+Fedora+Tech+Meeting

Hi Jared,

Thanks for the comment. I’ll add that meeting to my schedule and try to attend. I did read the PR before and while personally, I’m a little concerned about how <> and <.> can seem to represent different things based on what your {{PUT}}ing to, for this issue, I’m more concerned that for the binary resource

 <http://en.wikipedia.org/Cat> <http://schema.org/name> "Cat" .

in the ~ashley.art~fcr-desc.nt is instead represented as: 

  <http://localhost:8666/fcrepo/rest/ashley.art> <http://schema.org/name>   "Cat" .

in the GET request, which I don’t see how that’s part of the discussion for in that previous PR.
Ohhhhh, sorry I must have missed that. Okay I see what you are saying, I’ll have a look.
